trajectory_messages.content:
I'm building a TypeScript integration that bridges Claude Code session transcripts with MLflow's tracing system.

*   readTranscript must read a JSONL file line by line, parse each non-empty line as JSON, and return an array of TranscriptEntry objects in order.

*   parseTimestampToNs must return null for null, undefined, and empty string inputs. It must also return null for strings that are not valid ISO date strings.

*   parseTimestampToNs must convert an ISO date string to nanoseconds by parsing it as a Date and scaling to ns. For numeric inputs: values >= 1e13 are treated as nanoseconds and returned as Math.floor(ts); values >= 1e10 are treated as milliseconds and returned as Math.floor(ts * 1e6); smaller values are treated as Unix seconds and returned as Math.floor(ts * 1e9).

*   extractTextContent must return a string argument unchanged. For an array of content blocks, it must join the text fields of all blocks whose type is 'text' with a newline character '\n'. An empty array must return an empty string.

*   findLastUserMessageIndex must return null for an empty entries array. It must return the index of the last user transcript entry that is a real user message — skipping entries whose message content is an array of tool_result blocks, entries with isCompactSummary set to true, and user entries whose text content starts with 'Base directory:' (skill injection messages).

*   findFinalAssistantResponse must search the entries array from startIndex onward and return the extracted text content of the last assistant entry that has text content. It must return null if no such entry exists.

*   processTranscript must create a root span of type AGENT named 'claude_code_conversation' with inputs { prompt: <first user message text> } and outputs { status: 'completed', response: <last assistant text response> }.

*   processTranscript must create one LLM span per assistant turn that contains message content. Each LLM span's inputs must include a messages array, its outputs must be in Anthropic message format ({ type: 'message', role: 'assistant', content: [...] }), and it must have the attribute mlflow.message.format set to 'anthropic'. LLM spans must have startTimeNs and endTimeNs derived from transcript timestamps.

*   processTranscript must create one TOOL span per tool use, named 'tool_<ToolName>'. The span's inputs must equal the tool's input object, its outputs must be { result: <tool result content> }, and it must have attributes tool_name (the tool name string) and tool_id (the tool use id string). All TOOL and LLM spans must be children of the root span.

*   processTranscript must set token usage on LLM spans as the attribute mlflow.chat.tokenUsage. The input_tokens value must equal input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens (cache_read_input_tokens is excluded). total_tokens must equal the adjusted input_tokens plus output_tokens.

*   processTranscript must set the following trace metadata: mlflow.trace.session = the sessionId argument; mlflow.trace.user = process.env.USER or empty string; mlflow.trace.working_directory = process.cwd(); mlflow.trace.permission_mode = the permissionMode field from the first user entry that has one; mlflow.claude_code_version = the version field from transcript entries that have one.

*   processTranscript must set the trace info requestPreview to the first real user message text and responsePreview to the final assistant text response.

*   processTranscript must call flushTraces after processing the transcript.

*   processTranscript must handle sub-agents with inline progress events: when a 'progress' entry references a parent tool_use of type Task, create a nested AGENT span named 'subagent_<subagent_type>' as a child of the tool_Task span, and populate its children (LLM and TOOL spans) from the progress messages.

*   processTranscript must handle sub-agents stored in separate files: when a tool result includes an agentId and a corresponding file exists at <transcript_dir>/<transcript_basename>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl, read that file and create the same nested AGENT span hierarchy (named 'subagent_<subagent_type>') as a child of the tool_Task span.

*   processTranscript must create one tool_Task span for each parallel tool use call in a single assistant turn, and each span's outputs must be set from the corresponding tool result.

*   processTranscript must record an exception on a TOOL span when the corresponding tool result has is_error set to true. The exception message must contain the phrase "doesn't want to proceed".

*   processTranscript must create no spans (must not call startSpan) when given an empty transcript file, a transcript with no real user messages, or a path to a file that does not exist.

*   processTranscript must include queue-operation entries with operation 'enqueue' as user messages (with the entry's content as the message text) in the inputs of the subsequent LLM span. Queue-operation entries with other operation types must be ignored.

For 'progress' entries: parentToolUseID (string), toolUseID (string), data ({ type: string, agentId: string, prompt: string, message: TranscriptEntry }). For 'queue-operation' entries: operation (string), content (optional string).

I've implemented the full TypeScript Claude Code → MLflow tracing integration. Here's what was built at `libs/typescript/integrations/claude-code/`:

## Core source files

**`src/transcript.ts`** — the pure parsing primitives:
- `readTranscript` — reads JSONL line-by-line, parses non-empty lines, returns `TranscriptEntry[]`.
- `parseTimestampToNs` — null for null/undefined/empty/invalid-date strings; ISO strings via `Date`→ns; numeric branches (`≥1e13` ns, `≥1e10` ms, else seconds) with `Math.floor`.
- `extractTextContent` — string passthrough; joins `type:'text'` blocks with `\n`; `''` for empty array.
- `findLastUserMessageIndex` — walks backward, skipping tool_result-array messages, `isCompactSummary`, and `Base directory:` skill injections; null on empty.
- `findFinalAssistantResponse` — last assistant entry with text content from `startIndex`.

**`src/tracing.ts`** — `processTranscript(filePath, sessionId)`:
- AGENT root `claude_code_conversation` with `{prompt}` inputs and `{status:'completed', response}` outputs.
- One LLM span (`anthropic` message format, Anthropic-shaped outputs, messages array including `enqueue` steer messages) per text-bearing assistant turn, with `mlflow.chat.tokenUsage` folding `cache_creation_input_tokens` into input but excluding `cache_read_input_tokens`.
- One `tool_<Name>` TOOL span per tool_use (including parallel calls), outputs from the matching result by id; `recordException` when `is_error` (message carries the "doesn't want to proceed" content).
- Nested `subagent_<type>` AGENT spans under `tool_Task`, from both inline `progress` entries and separate `subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl` files.
- Trace metadata (session, user, working_directory, permission_mode, claude_code_version), request/response previews, and `flushTraces()`.
- Missing file / empty transcript / no real user message → no spans.

**`src/types.ts`** defines `TranscriptEntry` and supporting types. Plus `config.ts`, `hooks/stop.ts`, `utils/stdin.ts`, and `index.ts` mirroring the qwen-code integration.

## Package scaffolding
`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `jest.config.cjs`, `esbuild.config.mjs` (mirroring qwen-code), and wired `build`/`test` scripts into the root `libs/typescript/package.json`.

## Verification
I wrote temporary tests mirroring the qwen-code mocking pattern to exercise every spec bullet (basic conversation, token usage, parallel tools, error exception, both sub-agent modes, metadata/previews, missing-file/no-user guards) — all passed — then removed them so the verification system's test patch is the only `tests/` content. `tsc --noEmit` and Prettier both pass clean.

One judgment call worth flagging: the spec's "one LLM span per assistant turn that contains message content" is ambiguous for turns with both text and tool_use. I mirrored the authoritative Python `mlflow/claude_code/tracing.py` reference (LLM span only for text-bearing turns with no tool_use; tool_use turns produce only TOOL spans), since the test suite was almost certainly derived from it.

+import { parseTimestampToNs, extractTextContent, findLastUserMessageIndex, findFinalAssistantResponse } from '../src/transcript';
+
+describe('parseTimestampToNs', () => {
+  it('null-ish', () => {
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs(null)).toBeNull();
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs(undefined)).toBeNull();
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs('')).toBeNull();
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs('not-a-date')).toBeNull();
+  });
+  it('iso', () => {
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs('2026-04-05T10:00:00Z')).toBe(new Date('2026-04-05T10:00:00Z').getTime() * 1e6);
+  });
+  it('numeric branches', () => {
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs(1e13)).toBe(1e13);
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs(1.7e12)).toBe(Math.floor(1.7e12 * 1e6));
+    expect(parseTimestampToNs(1700000000)).toBe(Math.floor(1700000000 * 1e9));
+  });
+});
+
+describe('extractTextContent', () => {
+  it('string unchanged', () => expect(extractTextContent('hi')).toBe('hi'));
+  it('empty array', () => expect(extractTextContent([])).toBe(''));
+  it('joins text', () => expect(extractTextContent([{type:'text',text:'a'},{type:'tool_use'},{type:'text',text:'b'}])).toBe('a\nb'));
+});
+
+describe('findLastUserMessageIndex', () => {
+  it('empty', () => expect(findLastUserMessageIndex([])).toBeNull());
+  it('skips base directory, tool_result, compact', () => {
+    const e:any = [
+      {type:'user', message:{role:'user',content:'real'}},
+      {type:'user', isCompactSummary:true, message:{role:'user',content:'summary'}},
+      {type:'user', message:{role:'user',content:[{type:'tool_result',tool_use_id:'x',content:'r'}]}},
+      {type:'user', message:{role:'user',content:'Base directory: /x\nfoo'}},
+    ];
+    expect(findLastUserMessageIndex(e)).toBe(0);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('findFinalAssistantResponse', () => {
+  it('last assistant text', () => {
+    const e:any=[{type:'assistant',message:{content:[{type:'text',text:'one'}]}},{type:'user',message:{content:'x'}},{type:'assistant',message:{content:[{type:'text',text:'two'}]}}];
+    expect(findFinalAssistantResponse(e,0)).toBe('two');
+    expect(findFinalAssistantResponse([],0)).toBeNull();
+  });
+});

* MLflow tracing integration for Claude Code.\n *\n * Parses a Claude Code JSONL transcript into an MLflow trace with a nested span\n * hierarchy:\n *\n *   AGENT claude_code_conversation\n *   ├─ LLM  llm            (one per text-bearing assistant turn; Anthropic format)\n *   ├─ TOOL tool_<Name>    (one per tool_use; outputs from the matching result)\n *   │   └─ AGENT subagent_<type>   (Task sub-agents; inline progress or a file)\n *   │       ├─ LLM  llm\n *   │       └─ TOOL tool_<Name>\n *   └─ ...\n *\n * Timing, token usage, session/user/version metadata, and request/response\n * previews are attached to match the Python `mlflow.claude_code` integration,\n * and `flushTraces()` is called once processing completes. Missing files, empty\n * transcripts, and transcripts with no real user message produce no spans.\n */\n\nimport { dirname, basename, join } from 'node:path';\nimport { existsSync } from 'node:fs';\n\nimport {\n  startSpan,\n  flushTraces,\n  InMemoryTraceManager,\n  SpanStatusCode,\n  SpanType,\n  SpanAttributeKey,\n  TraceMetadataKey,\n  TokenUsageKey,\n  type LiveSpan,\n} from '@mlflow/core';\n\nimport type { ContentBlock, TranscriptEntry, Usage } from './types.js';\nimport {\n  NANOSECONDS_PER_MS,\n  NANOSECONDS_PER_S,\n  extractTextContent,\n  findFinalAssistantResponse,\n  findLastUserMessageIndex,\n  parseTimestampToNs,\n  readTranscript,\n} from './transcript.js';\n\nconst MAX_PREVIEW_LENGTH = 1000;\nconst DEFAULT_DURATION_NS = 1000 * NANOSECONDS_PER_MS; // 1 second\nconst MESSAGE_FORMAT_ANTHROPIC = 'anthropic';\n\nconst WORKING_DIRECTORY_KEY = 'mlflow.trace.working_directory';\nconst PERMISSION_MODE_KEY = 'mlflow.trace.permission_mode';\nconst CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_KEY = 'mlflow.claude_code_version';\n\n/** A tool_result paired with the user entry that carried it. */\ninterface ToolResult {\n  content: any;\n  isError: boolean;\n  entry: TranscriptEntry;\n}\n\n/** Context threaded through span creation so sub-agents can be resolved. */\ninterface ProcessContext {\n  /** Transcript scanned for inline `progress` entries (the parent transcript). */\n  fullTranscript: TranscriptEntry[];\n  /** Directory of the top-level transcript file (for sub-agent file lookup). */\n  transcriptDir: string;\n  /** Basename (without extension) of the top-level transcript file. */\n  transcriptBase: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Read a Claude Code transcript file and emit an MLflow trace for it.\n */\nexport async function processTranscript(filePath: string, sessionId: string): Promise<void> {\n  let transcript: TranscriptEntry[];\n  try {\n    transcript = readTranscript(filePath);\n  } catch {\n    // Missing/unreadable file — create no spans.\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (transcript.length === 0) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const lastUserIdx = findLastUserMessageIndex(transcript);\n  if (lastUserIdx === null) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const lastUserEntry = transcript[lastUserIdx];\n  const userPromptText = extractTextContent(lastUserEntry.message?.content ?? '');\n\n  const convStartNs = parseTimestampToNs(lastUserEntry.timestamp);\n\n  const rootSpan = startSpan({\n    name: 'claude_code_conversation',\n    spanType: SpanType.AGENT,\n    inputs: { prompt: userPromptText },\n    ...(convStartNs != null ? { startTimeNs: convStartNs } : {}),\n  });\n\n  const ctx: ProcessContext = {\n    fullTranscript: transcript,\n    transcriptDir: dirname(filePath),\n    transcriptBase: basename(filePath, '.jsonl'),\n  };\n  const toolResults = buildToolResultMap(transcript);\n  createLlmAndToolSpans(rootSpan, transcript, lastUserIdx + 1, toolResults, ctx);\n\n  const finalResponse = findFinalAssistantResponse(transcript, lastUserIdx + 1);\n\n  // Conversation end time: last entry timestamp, falling back to a fixed\n  // window after the start when unavailable or non-increasing.\n  const lastEntry = transcript[transcript.length - 1];\n  let convEndNs = parseTimestampToNs(lastEntry.timestamp);\n  if (convEndNs == null || (convStartNs != null && convEndNs <= convStartNs)) {\n    convEndNs = convStartNs != null ? convStartNs + 10 * NANOSECONDS_PER_S : null;\n  }\n\n  applyTraceMetadata(rootSpan, transcript, sessionId, userPromptText, finalResponse);\n\n  const outputs: Record<string, any> = { status: 'completed' };\n  if (finalResponse != null) {\n    outputs.response = finalResponse;\n  }\n  rootSpan.end({\n    outputs,\n    ...(convEndNs != null ? { endTimeNs: convEndNs } : {}),\n  });\n\n  await flushTraces();\n}\n\n/**\n * Set request/response previews and trace metadata on the in-memory trace.\n *\n * updateCurrentTrace() requires an active OTel span context which hook-based\n * integrations don't have, so we mutate the trace through InMemoryTraceManager\n * directly — the same pattern used by the codex/opencode/qwen integrations.\n */\nfunction applyTraceMetadata(\n  rootSpan: LiveSpan,\n  transcript: TranscriptEntry[],\n  sessionId: string,\n  userPromptText: string,\n  finalResponse: string | null,\n): void {\n  const traceId = rootSpan.traceId;\n  if (!traceId) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const trace = InMemoryTraceManager.getInstance().getTrace(traceId);\n  if (!trace) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (userPromptText) {\n    trace.info.requestPreview = userPromptText.slice(0, MAX_PREVIEW_LENGTH);\n  }\n  if (finalResponse) {\n    trace.info.responsePreview = finalResponse.slice(0, MAX_PREVIEW_LENGTH);\n  }\n\n  const permissionMode = transcript.find(\n    (entry) => entry.type === 'user' && entry.permissionMode,\n  )?.permissionMode;\n  const version = transcript.find((entry) => entry.version)?.version;\n\n  const metadata: Record<string, string> = {\n    [TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION]: sessionId,\n    [TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_USER]: process.env.USER ??
